breakfast.name: Gimbap (Korean Seaweed Rice Rolls)
breakfast.description: Popular Korean grab-and-go meal of seasoned rice rolled with vegetables and protein, sliced into rounds. Can be eaten warm or at room temperature with many regional variations
ingredients: 2 eggs, cooked into omelette and sliced
instructions: Cook short-grain rice and season while warm with sesame oil and salt
Blanch spinach, squeeze dry, then season with sesame oil and salt
Cook beef with soy sauce and sesame oil
Cook seasoned burdock root separately
Make thin omelette, cool, and slice into strips
Place bamboo sushi mat on work surface and lay nori sheet shiny side down
Spread approximately 1 cup warm seasoned rice evenly over nori (leave 3/4 inch at top)
Arrange fillings in horizontal line across center, starting with smaller ingredients
Roll tightly using mat, applying even pressure
Brush seam with water to seal
Remove mat and brush outside with sesame oil
Cut into 6-8 pieces using sharp, wet knife
Serve warm or at room temperature
breakfast.notes: Proper order of filling ingredients is crucial to keep stacked ingredients in place as you roll. Sesame oil is essential for authentic flavor
breakfast.fun_fact: Gimbap is the most popular grab-and-go meal in Korea and can be found everywhere with many regional variations. It's often made with different fillings depending on region and preference

items.name: Eggs, cooked into omelette and sliced

stepHelp: Season the rice while it's still warm so the sesame oil and salt absorb evenly — cold rice won't take the seasoning as well.
Squeeze out as much water as you can — wet spinach will make the rice soggy and the roll harder to seal.
Let it cool fully before slicing, or the strips will be too soft and tear when you roll.
Shiny side down means the matte, textured side faces up, which grips the rice better.
Wet your fingers slightly first so the rice doesn't stick to them, and leave that bare strip at the top — it's what seals the roll shut.
Smaller/flatter ingredients first, taller ones on top — this keeps the roll from bulging unevenly on one side.
Use the mat to curl the near edge over the filling first, then keep rolling forward while pressing down firmly and evenly — a loose roll falls apart when sliced.
A wet blade glides through instead of squashing the roll — wipe and re-wet the knife between cuts for clean slices.

variations.title: Tuna Gimbap
variations.text: Swap the beef for canned tuna mixed with a little mayo for a simpler, budget-friendly version.

variations.title: Kimchi Gimbap
variations.text: Add well-drained chopped kimchi to the filling line for a spicy, tangy kick.

variations.title: Vegetarian Gimbap
variations.text: Skip the beef and add more vegetables like cucumber, bell pepper, or seasoned tofu strips.

variations.title: Cheese Gimbap
variations.text: A modern favorite — add a thin strip of cheese alongside the other fillings for a melty twist while the roll is still warm.

variations.title: Mini Gimbap
variations.text: Use half-sheets of nori for smaller, snack-sized rolls — great for lunchboxes.

serveWith.intro: Gimbap is Korea's most popular grab-and-go food, and it holds up well next to a few simple sides.

items.title: Kimchi
items.text: The classic side — its tang and crunch complement the mild, savory rice roll.

items.title: Danmuji (Pickled Radish)
items.text: More pickled radish on the side echoes what's already inside the roll.

items.title: Miso or Doenjang Soup
items.text: A warm, savory soup rounds out gimbap into a full meal.

items.title: Fish Cake Soup
items.text: A common street-food pairing — the warm broth is a nice contrast to the cool rice roll.

items.title: Barley Tea
items.text: A light, roasted tea that cleanses the palate between bites.

expertTips.title: Season Every Component
expertTips.text: Each filling (spinach, beef, burdock) is seasoned on its own before assembly — this layering of flavor is what separates good gimbap from bland rice-and-stuff.

expertTips.title: Don't Overfill
expertTips.text: It's tempting to pack in more filling, but an overstuffed roll won't seal or slice cleanly — less is more.

expertTips.title: Roll With Confidence
expertTips.text: Firm, even pressure the whole way through the roll matters more than going slowly — hesitation makes the roll uneven.

expertTips.title: Sesame Oil on the Outside
expertTips.text: Brushing the finished roll with sesame oil adds shine, flavor, and helps keep it from drying out.

storage.title: Fridge
storage.text: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 day — rice hardens quickly when chilled, so gimbap is best eaten the day it's made.

storage.title: Room Temperature
storage.text: Fine to hold at room temperature for a few hours, which is part of why it's such a popular grab-and-go food.

storage.title: Freezer
storage.text: Not recommended — the rice texture suffers badly after freezing and thawing.

breakfast.makeAhead: Prep and season all the individual fillings (rice, spinach, beef, egg, burdock, radish) up to a day ahead and keep them separately in the fridge. Rolling only takes a few minutes once everything is ready, so you can assemble fresh gimbap quickly even on a rushed morning.

faqs.q: Why did my roll fall apart when I sliced it?
faqs.a: Most likely it wasn't rolled tightly enough, or the rice wasn't spread evenly. Make sure to apply firm, even pressure the whole way through the roll.

faqs.q: Can I make this without a bamboo mat?
faqs.a: A clean kitchen towel or a sheet of plastic wrap can work in a pinch, though a bamboo mat makes even pressure much easier to achieve.

faqs.q: Is gimbap the same as sushi?
faqs.a: They look similar but differ in seasoning — gimbap rice is seasoned with sesame oil and salt (no vinegar), and it's typically filled with cooked ingredients rather than raw fish.

faqs.q: How far ahead can I make the rice?
faqs.a: Cook and season the rice up to a few hours ahead, keeping it covered so it doesn't dry out, but avoid refrigerating it before rolling since cold rice gets hard and won't hold together as well.

lunch.name: Bibimbap (Korean Mixed Rice Bowl)
lunch.description: Mixed rice bowl with vegetables, beef and egg. Name means mixed rice, represents harmony of different ingredients
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (mushroom, spinach, zucchini, bean sprouts, carrot)
instructions: Season vegetables: sauté each separately with sesame oil, garlic, salt, keep warm
Season beef with soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, cook until done
Divide rice among bowls
Arrange vegetables and beef on top
Make indentation in center, crack raw egg into it
Top with gochujang and sesame seeds
Serve with bowl of hot broth on side
Mix everything together before eating
lunch.notes: Each vegetable should be seasoned separately for best flavor. Raw egg cooks from heat of rice
lunch.fun_fact: Bibimbap name means mixed rice, represents harmony of different ingredients in one bowl. Popular lunch throughout Korea

dinner.name: Korean Bulgogi (Korean BBQ Beef)
dinner.description: Thinly sliced beef marinated in sweet soy - Korean dinner favorite
ingredients: 600g beef sirloin, tenderloin or rib eye, very thinly sliced
instructions: Freeze beef 20-30 minutes to make slicing easier; slice very thinly
Combine soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, minced garlic, minced ginger, sugar, black pepper
Add grated pear; stir to combine
Add beef slices and onion to marinade; toss well
Marinate at least 30 minutes (overnight for deeper flavor)
Heat large skillet or grill pan over medium-high to high heat
Cook marinated beef 3-5 minutes per side until caramelized
Do not overcrowd pan; work in batches
Transfer to serving plate; garnish with sesame seeds and scallions
Serve immediately with steamed rice, kimchi, and ssamjang
dinner.notes: Pear enzymes tenderize beef while adding subtle sweetness
dinner.fun_fact: Pear is essential for tenderizing and creating flavor

dinner.name: Galbitang (Short Rib Soup)
dinner.description: Korean beef short rib soup with vegetables - warming and nourishing
instructions: Blanch beef short ribs in boiling water 5 minutes, drain and rinse
Bring fresh water to boil, add blanched ribs
Add ginger slices, bring back to boil
Reduce heat and simmer 40 minutes until ribs are tender
Add daikon radish, carrots, potatoes
Continue simmering 20 minutes until vegetables are tender
Add garlic, soy sauce, sugar
Simmer 10 more minutes
Add perilla leaves (or spinach), scallions
Drizzle with sesame oil
Season with salt and pepper
Serve hot in bowls
Garnish with roasted sesame seeds
dinner.notes: Blanching ribs removes impurities for clear broth. This is a nourishing family soup
dinner.fun_fact: Galbitang is often served on special occasions in Korea
